title: Annotatio IV §.VIII: Ambrose — consecration’s change in the symbols is only spiritual
pass_a_gloss: To Athanasius agrees the most eloquent of Sacred Rhetors toward the end of that age, namely S. AMBROSE, indicating that every mutation which belongs to the symbols of the Sacred Supper through their consecration is only spiritual, Book 4 On the Sacraments ch. 4. You yourself, he says, were, but an Old Creature; after you have been consecrated, you have begun to be a new creature. And again: You will perhaps say, my bread is ordinary; but this bread is bread before the words of the blessing of the sacraments; when consecration has come, from bread is made the body of Christ.
pass_b_english: Ambrose (De Sacr. 4.4), late in the century, agrees: every change that consecration works in the Supper’s symbols is only spiritual.
You yourself were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one. Ordinary bread before the blessing-words; when consecration comes, from bread is made Christ’s body.
source_text: Athanasio adstipulatur Rhetorum Sacrorum, circa exitum ejus Seculi, disertissimus, videl. S. AMBROSIUS, mutationem omnem quæ in symbola S. Cœnæ, per consecrationem eorum, competit, nonnisi spiritualem esse indigitans, Lib. 4. de Sacram. cap. 4. Tu ipse, inquit, eras, sed Vetus Creatura, postquam consecratus es, nova creatura esse cœpisti. Et iterum: Tu fortè dices, panis meus usitatus est; sed panis iste panis est, ante verba benedictionis sacramentorum, ubi accesserit consecratio, de pane fit corpus Christi.
notes: Ambrose: only spiritual mutation of symbols.
